digest.greeting: Good morning, Jean. Today is Monday, November 16. Seven meeting anchors and a protected noon block make the day busiest from 11:00 AM onward; six priority items carry forward, five urgent. First, use the 8:00 AM planning hour to approve timecards and lock the week, then close Amazon Connect Wave 2 readiness and the Product, Operations, and SMS decisions before the back-to-back pipeline and portfolio reviews. The clearest new risks are unresolved I-751 outreach scope and Amazon Connect call quality and monitoring ownership. Microsoft 365 access is healthy again. Dashboard state has not changed since Thursday, so completion signals may be stale.

items.label: Close Amazon Connect Wave 2 readiness
items.detail: All 12 offices are live and the nine transfer Omni flows are built, but activation, access validation, open RAID ownership, and the November 17 deployment sequence still need a clear go/no-go in today’s standup.

items.label: Close the Product handoff and communication gap
items.detail: Set the EPMO intake, initiation, prioritization, and escalation expectations, including ownership for IT stories and advance notice of workflow changes.

items.label: Close the Operations readiness decisions
items.detail: Confirm the RFE or Expansion taskset path, record the VAWA standalone readiness outcome, and decide whether today’s Production Compliance restart can proceed.

items.label: Confirm the SMS grooming and sprint plan
items.detail: Reconcile the Sprint 23 versus Sprint 25 sequence, complete the use-case story inventory, resolve English and Spanish template differences, and confirm Product, IT, architecture, and Marketing roles.

items.label: Review and sign the fake help-desk security alert
items.detail: Rippling is still waiting for Jean’s acknowledgment of the urgent phishing and fake help-desk notice. Complete it so the security communication can close.

items.label: Complete the EPMO Asana pain-points poll
items.detail: Only two responses were recorded Friday, and Sara asked everyone to respond by EOD today. Submit the poll before the team decides its next move away from Asana.

items.label: 8:00-9:00 AM - Approve timecards and prepare the week
items.detail: Use the early planning hour to clear timecards, set the week’s decision list, and prepare the highest-risk items before meetings begin.

items.label: 11:00 AM-noon - CM CoE alignment and Amazon Connect standup
items.detail: The meetings run back-to-back. Prioritize Phase 1 and 2 requests first, then use the standup for Wave 2 activation, access, call quality, and the remaining RAID owners.

items.label: Noon-1:00 PM - Protected focus block
items.detail: Preserve this hour to close decisions or update materials before the afternoon portfolio sequence.

items.label: 1:30-2:30 PM - IT pipeline and BD portfolio reviews
items.detail: Bring current priority changes, UAT status, new intake, target-date corrections, and material blockers; the meetings are back-to-back.

items.label: 3:00-5:00 PM - Maria 1:1 and LeadUp Module 4
items.detail: Use the 1:1 for portfolio roadblocks and next owners, then finish the day with the final 2026 LeadUp module. Colombia’s holiday may reduce availability for affected colleagues.

items.label: Approve timecards and lock the week’s decision list
items.detail: Use the 8:00 AM block to clear approvals, identify the decisions required from today’s meetings, and reserve the noon focus hour for the most consequential follow-through.

items.label: Clarify the I-751 outreach scope
items.detail: The email thread distinguishes legacy I-751 client outreach questions from the broader Universal Intake update targeted for Q1 2027. Confirm whether the legacy questions proceed separately and who owns the boundary decision.

items.label: Assign Amazon Connect call-quality and monitoring ownership
items.detail: Dallas reported background-noise quality concerns after a client complaint, while the standup thread says automated error monitoring is not yet defined. Decide the immediate mitigation and assign the longer-term monitoring effort before Wave 2 expands usage.

items.label: 9:30-11:00 AM - Jhara 1:1 and slide focus time
items.detail: Use the 1:1 for portfolio roadblocks, then protect the 10:00 AM block to prepare the EPMO weekly slides.

items.label: 11:30 AM-noon - CM CoE/Product and Amazon Connect conflict
items.detail: Two meetings overlap exactly. Choose coverage today so Product alignment and deployment support both have a clear owner.

items.label: 2:00-4:00 PM - EPMO leadership and Nicolas 1:1
items.detail: Bring portfolio risks, dependencies, and escalation decisions into the team-lead meeting, then close remaining ownership questions with Nicolas.
